primary.summary_en: The Feast of the Holy Innocents, observed on December 28 in the Roman Rite, commemorates the massacre of the young boys in Bethlehem ordered by King Herod. This day honors the infants as the first martyrs for Christ, celebrating their sacrifice and their baptism of blood.
primary.body_en:
The liturgy for the Feast of the Holy Innocents focuses on the infant martyrs killed by Herod the Great, as recorded in the Gospel of Matthew. These children, unable to speak in defense of their faith, are venerated as the earliest witnesses to Christ, symbolizing the cost of the Incarnation. In the 2026 liturgical calendar, this Feast is designated with the liturgical color red, signifying martyrdom.

As a Feast of the Lord and of the Blessed Virgin Mary, this day highlights the divine plan unfolding in infancy. The readings, though not explicitly cited in the simplified daily calendar, traditionally include the prophecy of Rachel weeping for her children. The Church presents these innocents as examples of pure innocence and sacrificial love, inviting the faithful to reflect on the mystery of innocent suffering and the sovereignty of God.
primary.confidence_note_en: The identity, date, and liturgical status are fixed in the 2026 USCCB calendar. The liturgical color red and the rank as Feast are officially confirmed.

app_hooks.hero_line_en: Honoring the First Martyrs: The Holy Innocents
app_hooks.prayer_prompt_en: Lord, we honor the Holy Innocents who died for Christ; teach us to offer our own innocence and sacrifice in love of You.
